snippet.title: Hunting For Kolkata's Tastiest Street Food 🇮🇳
snippet.description:
📍 Every place I've eaten, saved on a map. Five free in every country: https://somewheregood.io?s=yt-desc

In this video, I take you on a DIY food tour through the bustling streets of Kolkata. My adventure begins in the New Market area, where I immediately spot a crowd gathered around a popular sugarcane juice stall. For just 20 rupees, I grab a glass—and it’s one of the best sugarcane juices I’ve ever tasted.

Next, I stumble upon a vendor selling masala chai for only 5 rupees. I can’t resist, so I grab a glass and savor it right on the street. Continuing my walk, I find another vendor serving freshly squeezed orange juice for 50 rupees. It’s as refreshing as it is delicious.

With my thirst quenched, I cross the street in search of food and find a man cooking up fresh dosas. For just 35 rupees, I enjoy a crispy masala dosa while chatting with some locals.

Next, I hop into a classic yellow Kolkata taxi and head to KC Das for a famous rasgulla—a syrupy, cheese-filled dumpling that’s a must-try in the city. Afterward, I wander down a small alleyway and discover a shop selling kathi rolls. I chat with locals as I devour a chicken and egg roll, wrapping up my street food journey in true Kolkata style.

snippet.title: Pure Bihari Non Vegetarian Food I Dabbu Egg Poach + Champaran Style Mutton + Kadha Masala Chicken
snippet.description:
In this episode of Delhi Community Food Stories, we find ourselves in a warm, inviting home kitchen, immersed in the flavours and memories of a quintessential Bihari non-vegetarian feast. The host, a passionate professional and fellow food lover, brings together family recipes and everyday rituals in a meal that speaks of tradition, comfort, and community.

The experience began with a refreshing glass of saunf ka sharbat — subtly sweet, fragrant, and deeply nostalgic. As conversations flowed, we moved to the first dish of the day: dabbu poach, a beloved street food from Patna. Made in a ladle-like vessel known as a dabbu, this zesty egg snack was fun to prepare and even more fun to devour — a reminder of Bihar’s vibrant roadside food culture.

As the kitchen filled with aromas, preparations began for the main course. Mutton was set aside to marinate for a slow-cooked Champaran-style dish — bold, smoky, and spiced with intention. Meanwhile, a khada masala chicken came to life on the stove — a semi-dry dish infused with the deep fragrance of whole spices, offering warmth in every bite.

The meal continued with rohu fish marinated in a mustard, garlic, and red chilli paste. Cooked in a tomato-based gravy enriched with the classic mustard blend and tempered with panch phoran, the fish curry brought a beautiful balance of heat and tang. There were also crispy fish roe pakoras — a seasonal delicacy that added texture and surprise to the platter.

What unfolded over the next few hours was more than a cooking session. It was a window into the culinary culture of Bihar, where food is layered with stories, memories, and care. Each dish carried a distinct voice — some bold, some quiet — but all rooted in the idea of home.

This episode is a celebration of shared meals, everyday expertise, and the quiet pride that lives in home kitchens. Through spice-laden pots and heartfelt conversations, it offers a glimpse into how food continues to connect, comfort, and carry culture forward — one lovingly prepared plate at a time.

snippet.title: India's Best Butter Chicken is on the Streets of Delhi | Street Eats | Bon Appétit
snippet.description:
Bon Appétit joins Chef Meherwan Irani to explore Delhi’s street food scene at Aslam Chicken. Located in Old Delhi, Aslam Chicken is serving butter chicken–but it’s not the butter chicken you would expect. Grilled over charcoal on a rooftop, marinated with yoghurt and spices, this dish is finished off with a drenching of cream and astonishing amounts of butter. Considered the predecessor of the butter chicken we know so well, Old Delhi-style butter chicken perfectly showcases the skill, technique, and drama of Delhi street food.
